column3: Verify that the homepage loads correctly and displays all key elements.
column4:
1. Open Chrome. 
2. Navigate to https://www.boost.org. 
3. Observe load time and content. 
4. Check for logo, navigation bar, main content (e.g., welcome message), call-to-action buttons (e.g., "Get Started"), and footer. 
5. Click a call-to-action button.
column5: Homepage loads within 2 seconds, displays logo, navigation bar, main content, buttons, and footer without errors. Call-to-action redirects to the correct page (e.g., Libraries).
column7: High-priority: entry point for users. Test on multiple browsers.

column3: Ensure external links on the homepage are valid and open correctly.
column4:
1. Access homepage. 
2. Identify external links (e.g., to GitHub, boost.org). 
3. Click each link. 
4. Verify the target page loads.
column5: Links open in new tabs, target pages load without errors (e.g., GitHub loads https://github.com/boostorg).
column7: Medium-priority: supports user trust. Test all footer/external links.

column3: Validate that all navigation menu links redirect correctly.
column4:
1. Access https://www.boost.org. 
2. Locate navigation menu. 
3. Click each item (e.g., Libraries, Documentation, Downloads, Community, News). 
4. Verify URL and content of each page. 
5. Test dropdowns (if present) by hovering and clicking sub-items.
column5: Menu links redirect to correct pages (e.g., Libraries shows library list). Dropdowns function correctly. No 404 errors.
column7: High-priority: critical for site navigation. Test on desktop and mobile for responsiveness.

column3: Ensure navigation is usable on mobile devices.
column4:
1. Open https://www.boost.org/ on a mobile device (e.g., iPhone 12). 
2. Tap the hamburger menu.
3. Tap each menu item. 
4. Verify page loads and menu collapses after selection.
column5: Hamburger menu opens/closes smoothly, links redirect correctly, and menu collapses after selection.
column7: High-priority: mobile usability is critical. Test on iOS and Android.

column3: Verify that the Libraries page lists all Boost libraries.
column4:
1. Navigate to Libraries page. 
2. Check for a list of libraries (e.g., Boost.Asio, Boost.Beast). 
3. Verify pagination or "Load More" (if present). 
4. Click a library name.
column5: Page loads within 2 seconds, displays a complete list of libraries. Pagination/"Load More" works. Clicking a library redirects to its documentation.
column7: High-priority: core feature for developers. Compare with boost.org library list.

column3: Ensure library documentation is complete and functional.
column4:
1. Navigate to a library’s documentation (e.g., Boost.Beast). 
2. Verify sections: overview, API reference, examples. 
3. Click a code example’s "Copy" button (if present). 
4. Follow an internal link (e.g., to related library). 
5. Compare content with boost.org.
column5: Documentation loads within 2 seconds, includes all sections, code is copyable, internal links work, and content matches boost.org.
column7: High-priority: critical for developer use. Test examples like the chat server.

column3: Test documentation behavior with invalid or missing content.
column4:
1. Navigate to a non-existent library page (e.g., https://www.boost.org/libs/nonexistent). 
2. Access a library with known issues (if any, based on GitHub). 
3. Check for broken internal links.
column5: A 404 page displays for non-existent pages. Known issues are resolved or documented. Broken links are absent or redirect gracefully.
column7: Medium-priority: ensures robustness. Check GitHub issues for problematic libraries.

column3: Verify that search returns accurate results for valid inputs.
column4:
1. Locate search bar. 
2. Enter queries: "Boost.Beast", "WebSocket", "C++20". 
3. Press Enter or click search icon. 
4. Check result relevance and load time. 
5. Click top result.
column5: Results load within 3 seconds, are relevant (e.g., Boost.Beast links to its documentation), and top result redirects correctly.
column7: High-priority: critical for finding content. Test multiple query types.

column3: Test search with invalid or unusual inputs.
column4:
1. Access search bar. 
2. Test inputs: 
a) Empty query
b) Special characters (e.g., "@#$%")
c) Long query (100+ characters
d) Non-existent term (e.g., "xyz_library")
3. Submit each query.
column5: a) Empty query prompts "Please enter a term". b) Special characters return safe results or error. c) Long query processes without crashing. d) Non-existent term shows "No results".
column7: High-priority: ensures robustness and security. Creative test to prevent crashes.

column3: Verify search performance under high-latency conditions.
column4:
1. Use a network throttling tool (e.g., Chrome DevTools) to simulate 3G connection. 
2. Enter a query (e.g., "Boost.Asio"). 
3. Measure result load time. 
4. Check usability of results.
column5: Results load within 5 seconds on 3G, remain relevant, and are navigable.
column7: Medium-priority: ensures usability in poor network conditions.

column3: Ensure users can download the latest Boost release.
column4:
1. Navigate to Downloads page. 
2. Locate latest release link. 
3. Click download link. 
4. Verify file downloads. 
5. Check for instructions (e.g., OpenSSL for Boost.Beast).
column5: Download starts immediately, file matches expected size/format (e.g., .zip). Instructions are clear and include prerequisites.
column7: High-priority: core feature for library access. Verify file integrity.

column3: Verify access to previous Boost releases.
column4:
1. Navigate to Downloads page. 
2. Locate a previous release (e.g., Boost 1.85.0). 
3. Click download link. 
4. Verify file downloads.
column5: Download starts, file matches expected size/format.
column7: Medium-priority: supports legacy users. Test at least two older releases.

column3: Test behavior for broken or unavailable download links.
column4: 1. Navigate to Downloads page. 2. Click a known broken link (if identified via GitHub) or simulate a server error. 3. Observe response.
column5: A user-friendly error message displays (e.g., "File unavailable"). No site crash occurs.
column7: Medium-priority: ensures graceful error handling. Check GitHub for reported issues.

column3: Validate that community links are functional.
column4:
1. Navigate to Community page. 
2. Click links to GitHub issues
